root_idea.summary: The root has two principal orientations: distance or remoteness, and forceful attrition that reduces something toward wearing out or disintegration.
root_idea.development: The attrition sense extends to pounding, pulverizing, effacing, wearing out, drying up, and wasting; the distance sense extends to remoteness and height beyond reach.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed as the Quranic adjective citation form سَحِيقٌ.
Displayed as the Quranic noun citation form سُحْقٌ.

senses.usage_conditions: Used adjectivally; in the attested Quranic occurrence it describes a remote place.

senses.definition: Remoteness or alienation; in the fixed imprecation, “away with” or “may he be cast far away.”
senses.usage_conditions: Used in the imprecatory construction سُحْقًا لِـ, expressing a wish that someone be distanced from good, prosperity, or mercy.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bruise, bray, pound, or pulverize something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a solid thing or medicine; the action may be coarse, fine, or repeated.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of wind, to scour away, efface, or abrade the surface of the ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: May describe the removal of traces and the carrying away of broken particles or dust.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To wear a garment out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A garment is the explicitly attested object of this usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To render a hard thing soft or smooth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively of a hard object.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To destroy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended or figurative use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To kill a louse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the specific expression سَحَقَ القَمْلَةَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shave the head.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression سَحَقَ رَأْسَهُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the eye, to spend or shed its tears.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an eye and its tears.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a garment, to become old and worn out.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive usage describing the condition of a garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be distant or remote.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a thing or place; the associated noun سُحْقٌ denotes distance or remoteness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a palm tree, to become tall.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The height may be associated with a smooth trunk.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an animal, to run vehemently.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The attested usage refers to a pace between ordinary walking and the more rapid gait called حُضْر, with variant comparisons in the lexical description.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Mutual sexual rubbing between women.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A post-classical usage and a specialized application of rubbing together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove someone far away, alienate, or estrange him, including from mercy.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used transitively, including in a usage said of God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel’s foot, to become smooth with a degree of hardness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive usage applied specifically to a camel’s foot.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an udder, to lose its milk and become wasted, dried up, or shrunken.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of an udder after its milk has gone away.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a bucket, to become empty of its contents.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive usage applied to a bucket.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rubbing together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A reciprocal or mutual-action verbal noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be bruised, brayed, or pounded.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A quasi-passive or intransitive result corresponding to سَحَقَ in its pounding sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a garment, to become worn out, threadbare, or napless.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description may apply even to a garment that is new but has lost its nap.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a place, to be wide or ample.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An intransitive usage applied to a place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of tears, to be shed or pour forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of tears as a flowing discharge.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An old, worn-out, thin, or threadbare garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used as a prefixed noun in phrases such as سَحْقُ ثَوْبٍ; the plural is سُحُوقٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A worn or debased coin.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An extended usage, explicitly applied to a bad or counterfeit dirham.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pastor’s bag.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specific nominal usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Thin clouds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative usage comparing the clouds to an old, worn-out garment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The white mark or scar left on a camel’s back after a gall or sore has healed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of the healed, whitened place on the camel’s back.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Baldness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a dialectal usage of Yemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Tall or long, especially tall and advanced in age.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to palm trees and also to male or female asses; it may describe a tall man, woman, or long legs. For a palm, it can imply height placing its fruit far above the gatherer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bruised, brayed, pounded, or pulverized.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Explicitly applied to substances such as musk and saffron.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A vehement rain that sweeps away what lies in its path.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Describes a rain of large drops that is intense but of limited breadth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who engages in sexual rubbing with another woman.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized epithet described as blameworthy; its plural is سَحَّاقَاتٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Greatly distant or remote.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in the expression سُحْقٌ سَاحِقٌ, “great distance or remoteness.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Bald.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a dialectal usage of Yemen.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An instrument used for bruising, braying, or pounding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A tool noun referring to an implement by which something is pulverized.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Wide or ample.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival usage applied to a place or expanse.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of tears, pouring or streaming forth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Equivalent in the cited usage to flowing or forcefully discharged tears.

lane_unit_coverage.note: The remote or distant adjective sense is represented by the Quranic form.
